disclaimer: All scenarios are fictional. No commands run against devices or networks.

labs.title: Recognize a safe computer workflow
labs.context: You have downloaded an unfamiliar attachment from a mock email. Decide which actions protect your device and data.
steps: A file is named invoice.pdf.exe. What do you do?
Treat it as a possible executable and verify its source
The final extension can signal an executable. A filename is not evidence of safety.
A basic calculator requests contact access. Your response?
Deny and ask why the access would be needed
Permissions should fit a documented task.
You want to protect important study notes against accidental deletion. Choose a control.
Keep a separate tested versioned backup
A separate backup can restore data after a synced deletion.

labs.title: Read a simulated Linux terminal
labs.context: You're in an isolated sample home directory, not a real machine. Interpret basic read-only commands.
steps: Two dots refer to the parent.
The -a option includes entries hidden from default listings.
You see an unfamiliar file owned by another user. What's the safe action?
Viewing another user's data requires proper authorization.

labs.title: Protect a small organization
labs.context: A fictional company is setting up employee accounts and recovery controls.
steps: No passwords and no alternate controls
Unique passwords and MFA reduce compromise risk.
An employee changes departments. What should happen?
Least privilege should reflect current duties.
A suspicious login page arrives by text. What should staff do?
Use a known official login route
The company has backups but never tests restores. What is missing?
Test restores establish whether recovery works.

labs.title: Windows security triage
labs.context: A hypothetical workstation is slow following an ordinary system update. Choose a careful investigation path.
steps: Task Manager shows high CPU. First step?
High CPU is an observation rather than a diagnosis.
A standard employee needs to browse reports. Appropriate permission?
Least privilege limits mistakes and damage.
A system update is pending on a business computer. Best plan?
Updates benefit from planning and verification.

labs.title: Troubleshoot a fictional network
labs.context: A small office can connect to Wi-Fi, but a training website fails to load. No traffic is sent in this lab.
steps: A device has no assigned IP address. What might need checking?
An IP address is reachable but a site name fails. Investigate?
Name resolution is distinct from reachability.
The guest network can reach payroll records. What is the concern?
Visitor traffic should generally be separated from sensitive systems.
A host ignores ping. Does that prove it is offline?
ICMP filtering can block echo replies on healthy hosts.

labs.title: Trace beginner programming logic
labs.context: Interpret pseudocode running entirely inside this training page.
steps: Set count=2, then count=count+1. The result?
The assignment increases the value by one.
If locked=true, which branch runs in 'if locked then deny else allow'?
The true branch performs the denial.
A loop runs once for each of 4 mock log entries. How many iterations?
A client changes a displayed role to admin. What must protect the data?

labs.title: Analyze a fictional sign-in timeline
labs.context: Mock records: 09:00 login_failed user A; 09:01 login_failed user A; 09:02 login_success user B; 09:05 software deployment began. No real accounts are involved.
steps: Which event shows confirmed successful authentication?
Only the success event confirms the recorded authentication outcome; it does not prove broader compromise.
What is justified about user A?
Failures alone do not establish intent or account compromise.
Compare timestamps with the deployment change record
Correlating approved operational change information avoids premature conclusions.
Two failures for A, one success for B, and a later deployment; root cause unknown

labs.title: Make a cloud access decision
labs.course: Applied Security Architecture and Threat Modeling
labs.context: A fictional training portal stores private grades in a cloud database. A browser requests a grade record using a student ID.
steps: Where must the access decision occur?
At the trusted API or database security layer
Client-side controls can be changed by users.
A student asks for another student's record. What should happen?
Return it because the caller logged in
Use the identifier as proof of permission
Authentication alone is not resource authorization.
What is safe to include in an access-denied log?
Time, anonymized account ID, outcome, resource category
Log enough to investigate without exposing secrets.
The service goes offline. What should the team use?
An approved recovery and communication plan

labs.title: Defensive cryptography decisions
labs.context: A fictional organization needs confidential file storage, verified software downloads, and trusted internal messaging.
steps: What primarily protects a lost laptop's stored records?
Encryption protects confidentiality of stored data.
A publisher provides a trusted file digest. What can it help check?
Whether the file is free of every bug
Compare against an authentic, trusted hash reference.
Which property does a digital signature add?
Verification of origin and integrity under trusted keys
Signatures verify authenticity and integrity but do not themselves encrypt content.
A private key is exposed publicly. What is the priority?
Revoke or rotate it and investigate exposure

labs.title: Respond to a simulated supplier fraud alert
labs.context: Mock invoice email requests a bank change for a $45,000 payment. The sender display name is familiar, but the domain has one extra character.
steps: The sender domain differs from the established one
The payment amount has a comma
How should finance verify the request?
Use an existing trusted contact method
Call the number in the suspicious message
Report through approved channels and retain relevant message details
What should a leadership memo include?
Evidence, payment delay tradeoff, verification control and decision owner
A certain accusation of the supplier
A professional memo communicates grounded tradeoffs and actions.

labs.title: Scope an ethical testing engagement
labs.context: An organization grants written permission to review a synthetic application in an isolated classroom environment only.
steps: A production server shares the same brand. Is it in scope?
No, permission must explicitly include it
Yes, any related domain is allowed
Scope is defined by the authorization.
What makes a useful test hypothesis?
A specific expected access rule and a permitted way to check it
A plan to copy private data
A claim that every endpoint is vulnerable
Hypotheses should be narrow and falsifiable.
A mock lab result suggests improper access. What next?
Record the minimum allowed evidence and report it
Data minimization and approved reporting protect others.
When can the finding be closed?
When the patch is merely proposed
Closure should be based on verification.
